title: Felix Manz (1527)
hookLine: baptized as adults, an early Anabaptist martyr is drowned by other Protestants

lines: A BOAT ON THE RIVER IN ZURICH.
ONE STEP FURTHER THAN THE CITY.
cards: A small boat pushes out into the river that runs through Zurich. In it is a young man with his hands bound: Felix Manz. He had studied with Zwingli, read the Bible with him, cheered the questions Zwingli raised.
And he took those questions one step further than the city would allow. Now the city council of Zurich, a Protestant council in a Protestant city, has sentenced him to be drowned.
The accounts say he sang as they took him out. Today's word is the name opponents gave him and his friends: Anabaptist.

teach.b: Here's the step. Manz and a circle of friends, Conrad Grebel among them, read the New Testament and noticed that baptisms there follow faith. People hear, believe, then are baptized.
So shouldn't baptism come after a person can confess faith for themselves? They began baptizing one another as adults, in a house in Zurich.
Opponents called them Anabaptists, re-baptizers, since they'd been baptized as infants. They didn't accept the name; to them, this was their first real baptism. The council outlawed it.
Manz was arrested, released, arrested again, and finally drowned in the river.
Christians still answer the baptism question differently, and both answers have deep roots.
Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican and Methodist churches baptize infants, seeing baptism as God's gift and promise, given before a child can ask.
Mennonites, Baptists and others baptize those who confess faith themselves. Manz's circle held something else too.
They refused to take up the sword, even to defend themselves, and early Anabaptist confessions said so plainly.

teach.h: THE WOLF SHALL DWELL WITH THE LAMB.
teach.b: Their picture came from Isaiah, who sees a world where, in the King James words, "The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb," and "They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain." The peaceable kingdom.
It's hard to sit with. In those years, Christians put other Christians to death over how and when to baptize.
Manz was killed by a city whose reformers had once read the Bible beside him, and he went to the river still believing Jesus' followers should never hurt anyone.

how: Mennonite, Amish, Hutterite and other Anabaptist-descended churches baptize those who confess faith for themselves and remember their early martyrs, including Felix Manz, and nonviolence is part of their heritage.

games.q: you're Felix Manz. the Zurich council has outlawed adult baptism. you've been arrested and released. what do you do?
o: keep quiet and go back to the city church.
games.why: he kept going, was arrested again, and was drowned in the river. the accounts say he sang on the way.

practice: Start with Felix Manz in the boat, then widen it: Anabaptists, Catholics, Protestants, Orthodox Christians, who in more than one place and time have suffered at the hands of other Christians, and some still do.
Hold them in mind without needing to decide who was most to blame. If you pray, pray for them and for those who hurt them; if you don't, keep them company in silence.

wordCard.voice: Anabaptist. A name opponents gave to Christians who baptized adults on their own confession of faith. Felix Manz's circle also refused the sword.

orig.note: Greek: to dip or immerse; the New Testament's word for baptize.
